analysis.title: Global Economic Weekly: After the Blue Tsunami
key_insights: BofA reads the US midterms as a referendum on the second Trump administration, with the Democratic result stronger than a Blue Wave. It lists implications for the AI buildout, the Iran conflict, the debt limit, spending and deficits, immigration and the Fed.

Democratic wins in states where data center buildout is concentrated (Texas, Ohio, Georgia governors) point to more local data center regulation. BofA says this could slow the AI buildout and capex cycle, two recent pillars of US growth, and the stock market has sold off since the election.

BofA sees a silver lining in a slower AI buildout. If the sector is prone to overinvestment, a slowdown could lower the risk of a sharper contraction later, limit recession risk and reduce pressure on the Fed to hike.

On the US economics side, BofA argues regulation will raise investment costs but is not what breaks the capex cycle. Capex booms end when demand growth stops outpacing supply growth, and for now demand indicators support aggressive capex plans.

BofA's equity strategy team proposes tracking AI-related revenue against AI-related capex. Estimates suggest AI revenue growth starts to exceed capex growth as early as 3Q 2027, which can justify the close to 350GW of planned or under-construction data center capacity.

BofA does not expect more regulation to affect the nearly 70GW of data center power under construction. It keeps its forecast that AI investment contributes 30-50bp to US growth next year, and notes hyperscalers have again raised 2027 capex expectations.

Power and utilities research (Ross Fowler) argues the election results in Florida, Louisiana, North Dakota and Oklahoma are positive for the sector, so tighter rules in Texas, Georgia or Ohio could shift projects to other states.

A tighter US regulatory environment for AI could marginally help China in the AI race. Countries such as Canada, the Nordics, India, Mexico and Brazil could benefit if data center construction is diverted from the US.

Oil fell after the election as markets priced a higher chance of an Iran deal. BofA thinks the move may be unwarranted because a resolution still looks elusive, though escalation risk has become less prominent.
Affordability was a central election theme. Inflation has outpaced wage growth for two years, including for job stayers, and the labor share of income is at record lows.
BofA expects debt limit negotiations next year to be protracted, with Democratic priorities such as healthcare spending and data center regulation possibly traded for higher defense spending.

BofA sees structural US deficits of about 6% of GDP as unsustainable. Entitlement cuts look even less likely after the election, so higher taxes, most likely on high-income individuals, are the path of least resistance. A VAT is the efficient option but is likely to be skipped.

Democratic control of the Senate means future Trump nominees to the Fed Board can be blocked, which BofA says should strengthen Fed independence. The first test may be when Powell's term as Governor expires.

The affordability focus may support a stronger price stability mandate and a more hawkish Fed reaction function. BofA's base case remains two further Fed hikes, in December and March, with resilient growth.
BofA sees two possible policy paths: a more proactive Fed tightening against inflation, or an AI slowdown that brings cooler growth, inflation and rates.
The size of the Democratic win limits the risk of a major US trade policy escalation in 2027. Texas becoming the key swing state for Republicans could help Canada and Mexico in USMCA renegotiations.

Riksbank hiked 25bp to 2% as expected and kept its September rate path, which implies further tightening in 1H27. BofA expects one more 25bp hike in 1Q27, most likely February, for a 2.25% terminal rate, and sees a short cycle that is less hawkish than the market.

The Riksbank plans to borrow about SEK200bn to finance part of its FX reserves, with about SEK100bn potentially relevant for spot SEK purchases. The operation starts in 2027 and runs 12-18 months, with details due 16 December. BofA sees modest upside risk for SEK.

Norges Bank held at 4.5% with a tightening bias and a higher-for-longer signal. BofA thinks the rate has peaked, though high energy prices could still bring one more hike by 1Q27. Falling energy prices after the US election are the bigger NOK driver, and an Iran peace deal would disproportionately favor NOK downside.
A ceasefire could push oil and gas back to surplus and drive Brent toward $80/bbl or lower on average next year, according to BofA's energy team.

The BoE hiked 25bp as expected but BofA calls it a hawkish hike. The vote was 8-1 with one vote for 50bp, the MPC said policy is not on a pre-set path, and Pill and Lombardelli opened the door to near-term action.

BoE central projection, based on market pricing of four hikes, has inflation peaking at 4.9% in Q2 2027 and falling to 1.8% in the medium term. The MPC raised 2026 growth to 1.6% and 2027 growth to 1.3%.

Dovish elements at the BoE include Bailey saying this is not the first of an inevitable sequence of hikes, risk premium in the curve, medium-term inflation at 1.8%, and Taylor and Dhingra framing their hike votes as insurance.

BofA expects a second BoE hike in February to 4.25% unless the conflict resolves, and says the risk of a December move has risen. It also sees a risk of a third hike, but views market pricing of four total hikes as excessive.

Japan's FY27 Shunto is off to a strong start. Rengo targets a headline raise centered on 6% and base-pay raises centered on 4%, up from prior floors of 5% and 3%. BofA still expects base-pay raises near the recent 3.5% pace with upside risks.

A move toward 4% Shunto base-pay raises would raise BoJ overshoot concerns. BofA expects three more 25bp BoJ hikes in December 2026, March 2027 and July 2027, with a risk that the terminal rate goes above 2%.

BofA expects CEMAC to secure IMF regional financing assurances by year-end with or without Cameroon. It expects a staff-level agreement for Congo in Q4 2026 and for Gabon by Q1 2027, but not for Cameroon by year-end.
Central African regional debt markets are near their limits. Banks hold about a third of their balance sheets in sovereign bonds and Gabon pays all-in yields of 12-15%.

Brazil's R$405bn campaign package headline overstates the fiscal cost. BofA estimates R$157bn from committed measures (R$92bn in 2026 and R$65bn in 2027) because credit envelopes are not direct spending and disbursements lag.
Brazil's fiscal position remains delicate despite the smaller cost. Several measures are permanent, and BofA estimates a primary surplus of about 3.0% of GDP is needed to stabilize gross debt.
earnings_insights: Hyperscaler AI-related revenue growth (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Meta advertising, Oracle cloud) continued to climb as of 11/5/2026, per BofA US Equity and Quant Strategy using Visible Alpha data. These are reported results in the Q3 2026 season.

BofA equity strategy noted hyperscalers were penalized for any softness in results this earnings season, yet hyperscalers have not backed off capex plans and 2027 capex expectations were revised higher again.
BofA US Equity and Quant Strategy estimates AI-related revenue growth exceeds AI-related capex growth as early as 3Q 2027. This is an estimate, not a reported figure.

risk_factors: Local and state data center regulation in Texas, Ohio and Georgia could slow the AI buildout and capex cycle.
AI monetization: hyperscalers have been penalized for softness, and a capex bust depends on demand growth failing to outpace supply growth.
Persistently high US real interest rates from deficits around 6% of GDP and an unsustainable debt trajectory.
Protracted US debt limit negotiations next year.
An Iran resolution remaining elusive, with oil having fallen on deal hopes ahead of any actual agreement.
UK second-round inflation effects and energy prices, which could bring a December BoE hike or a third hike.
Sweden: geopolitical uncertainty, high energy prices and a laggard labor-market recovery, with risk of one more Riksbank hike in 2Q27.
Japan: Shunto base-pay settlements moving toward 4% would raise BoJ overshoot risk.
CEMAC: debt audit and GDP rebasing in Gabon could slip the staff-level agreement into Q2, and sovereign debt markets are saturated.
Brazil: permanent spending increases on already limited fiscal space, and a Finance Minister and Lula mandate that are still unknown.
charts_described: Exhibit 3: S&P 500 -1.2%, Nasdaq 100 -3.7% and semiconductors -8.5% from Sep 1 to election day, versus -2.8%, -5.5% and -14.0% since election day.
Exhibit 4 (NBC News): AI and data centers were crucial to 23% of voters, a major factor for 33%, a minor factor for 31% and not a factor for 13%.
Exhibit 8: Swedish underlying inflation (CPIF excluding energy and temporary fiscal measures) was 1.6% in September and the Riksbank expects it to rise above 2% next year.
Exhibit 12: BoE central projection has inflation peaking at 4.9%, with a weaker demand scenario and an adverse inflation scenario shown alongside.
Exhibit 13: Shunto base-pay hikes have held around 3.5% for three years running.
Exhibit 14: Rengo base-pay realization ratio has risen to around 80%.
vol_and_positioning: For SEK, positioning was considerably shorter SEK during the 2023 Riksbank hedging program, which suggests the impact of the new 2027 reserve-financing operation could be smaller this time.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict: the midterms are read as a referendum on the war, markets price a higher chance of a deal, and BofA says resolution still looks elusive with energy prices a key swing factor for Europe.
US-China AI race: tighter US AI regulation would tend to benefit China at the margin, while aligned countries could gain diverted data center construction.
US trade policy: BofA sees limited scope for escalation after the Democratic sweep, and USMCA renegotiation may favor Canada and Mexico as Texas gains weight for Republicans.
CEMAC region: IMF programs for Gabon, Congo and Cameroon, regional financing assurances and extractive-sector FX repatriation talks.
Brazil: post-election fiscal outlook and the next Finance Minister under Lula.

tension_points.bull_case: Regulation raises costs but does not cancel projects. Demand justifies planned capex, AI revenue growth is expected to exceed capex growth as early as 3Q 2027, and nearly 70GW under construction is unaffected, so AI investment adds 30-50bp to growth next year.
tension_points.bear_case: 76% of voters oppose local data centers and 40 of 41 opposing ballot measures passed. Tighter rules in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, which hold 35% of capacity under construction, plus monetization worries and a selloff (semis -14% since election) threaten the capex cycle.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Demand growth no longer outpacing supply growth, or AI-related revenue growth failing to start exceeding capex growth around 3Q 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: An AI slowdown brings cooler growth, inflation and interest rates, which lowers the pressure on the Fed to hike.
tension_points.bear_case: A stronger price stability mandate after the affordability election makes the Fed more proactive, with BofA's base case of hikes in December and March and deficits of about 6% of GDP keeping real rates high.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A breakdown in the AI trade or another shock triggering an economic slowdown would change the high real interest rate path.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil is falling because markets price a higher probability of a deal after the election, and a ceasefire could push Brent toward $80/bbl or lower on average next year.
tension_points.bear_case: BofA thinks the move lower in oil may be unwarranted because a resolution still seems elusive.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A US-Iran ceasefire or peace deal that returns oil and gas markets to surplus.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: 8-1 vote, no pre-set path, Pill and Lombardelli open to near-term action, and inflation projected to peak at 4.9% in Q2 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Dovish case: Bailey said this is not an inevitable sequence, medium-term inflation at 1.8% pushes back on four-hike pricing, and Taylor and Dhingra framed their votes as insurance.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Higher energy prices or upside data surprises would make a December hike live, while an Iran resolution or low second-round effects would hold BofA to one more hike in February.

tension_points.bull_case: Rengo's 4% base-pay guidance, CPI above 3% in early 2027 and strong profits and labor shortages could lift Shunto base-pay hikes toward 4%, raising BoJ overshoot risk.
tension_points.bear_case: Rengo's higher benchmark partly catches up with actual demands (5.94% demanded versus 5.01% settled in FY26) and UA Zensen kept its guidance unchanged, so 3.5% could hold.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Base-pay demands rising across sectors and employers signaling willingness to agree, seen in major company and JAW announcements from late November to early December.

tension_points.bull_case: The R$405bn headline overstates the cost. Credit envelopes are not spending, disbursements lag and several measures need congressional approval.
tension_points.bear_case: Many measures are permanent, raising the expenditure base beyond 2027, with Brazil needing a primary surplus near 3.0% of GDP to stabilize debt.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Not stated by the report beyond the next Finance Minister and Lula's mandate being key to the outlook.
